title: Feature flags + staged rollout plan for auto-rollback on SLO breach
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Goal
Define gating flags, staged rollout cohorts, and explicit criteria to expand rollout for the new auto-rollback-on-SLO-breach feature. Include a rollback plan for the feature itself (i.e., turning off auto-rollback safely and restoring prior behavior).

Context
Auto-rollback is safety-critical (can revert traffic splits automatically). We need conservative rollout gates, clear stop conditions, and an immediate kill-switch. We also need to avoid mass rollback events across many tenants due to monitor outages or labeling bugs.

Feature flag strategy (control plane)
All flags below are evaluated in rollout-controller. Naming convention aligned with existing RC flags.

1) Kill switch (highest priority)
- Flag: rc.auto_rollback.global_disable
- Default: true (disabled)
- Behavior: when true, SLO evaluator may compute verdicts but rollback executor must NOT apply any changes. Console should show "Auto-rollback disabled by flag".

2) Enable SLO verdict computation (no actions)
- Flag: rc.auto_rollback.verdicts_enabled
- Default: false
- Behavior: fetch monitors + evaluate policy, write decision trace + internal metrics. No rollback action.
- Purpose: validate monitor identity contract + evaluation correctness at scale before any automated actions.

3) Enable rollback execution (actions)
- Flag: rc.auto_rollback.execution_enabled
- Default: false
- Behavior: allow rollback executor to revert canary/AB split per policy.
- Guard: requires rc.auto_rollback.verdicts_enabled=true (hard dependency).

4) Notification gating
- Flag: rc.auto_rollback.notifications_enabled
- Default: false
- Behavior: incident-bot notifications (Slack/on-call) for auto rollback events.
- Note: keep off initially to avoid paging noise while we validate verdict quality.

5) Per-tenant allowlist (cohorts)
- Flag: rc.auto_rollback.tenant_allowlist
- Type: dynamic config list
- Default: empty
- Behavior: auto-rollback only executes if tenant_id is in allowlist (in addition to other flags).

6) Per-route allowlist (optional, for high-risk routes)
- Flag: rc.auto_rollback.route_allowlist
- Type: dynamic config list of route IDs (or route name)
- Default: empty
- Behavior: if set, only allowed routes can execute rollback; verdicts still computed for all.

7) Fail-open vs fail-closed behavior under monitor outage
- Flag: rc.auto_rollback.monitor_outage_mode
- Values: unknown_verdict (default), fail_closed
- Default: unknown_verdict
- Behavior:
  - unknown_verdict: treat monitor fetch errors/staleness as "UNKNOWN" and do not rollback.
  - fail_closed: treat as hard unhealthy (NOT recommended for initial rollout; keep for future controlled experiments).
- Note: aligns with hotfix guardrail work (see PR-18546).

Staged rollout cohorts
We will roll out in two dimensions:
- Phase A: compute verdicts only (no execution)
- Phase B: enable execution (auto rollback)

Cohort definitions (proposed)
C0 - Dev/Local
- Environment: staging + a single prod “shadow” route if available
- Flags: verdicts_enabled=true, execution_enabled=false
- Scope: internal test tenants only

C1 - Internal canary tenants (prod)
- Tenants: Redwood internal dogfood + low-traffic internal services
- Flags: verdicts_enabled=true, execution_enabled=false for 48 hours; then execution_enabled=true
- Allowlist: explicit tenant IDs

C2 - Low-risk hosted API tenants
- Criteria: token volume moderate, not Private/Dedicated, no custom routing overrides, stable monitor labeling
- Flags: enable execution per-tenant allowlist
- Limit: max N tenants/day (rate-limited expansion), and global cap on rollbacks/hour (executor-level; tracked in ENG-2315)

C3 - Dedicated (by agreement)
- Tenants: 1–3 dedicated customers with SRE/CS alignment
- Additional constraints: per-region thresholds enabled; ensure their monitors exist per region/tier

C4 - Broad hosted (default-on for eligible tenants)
- Eligibility: monitor coverage >= 99%, evaluator lag within bounds, false positives below threshold
- Flags: execution_enabled=true globally; tenant_allowlist removed or replaced with tenant_blocklist

C5 - Private/VPC
- Out of scope for initial default-on. Requires explicit customer opt-in and additional change management, plus verifying their telemetry path and monitor availability.

Expansion criteria / SLOs for the feature itself
We should only expand phases when all criteria hold for the prior cohort over the evaluation period.

Phase A (verdicts-only) exit criteria
- Monitor fetch success rate >= 99.9% for cohort routes over 24h
- Monitor freshness: 99% of queries return data newer than 2x scrape interval (or within agreed freshness bound)
- Evaluator lag p95 < 30s (time between window end and verdict computed)
- "UNKNOWN" verdict rate < 0.5% of evaluations for cohort routes (excluding planned monitor maintenance)
- Cardinality/label validation: no >1% of evaluations missing route/model/region/tier identity (ties to ENG-2322 + INT-3310)

Phase B (execution) exit/expand criteria
- Auto-rollback precision (proxy):
  - <= 1 rollback/day per tenant on average OR clearly attributable to real incidents (validated via post-rollback review)
  - <= 1 false-positive rollback/week across cohort (requires manual triage tagging in incident channel)
- Flapping control:
  - No tenant experiences rollback -> re-rollout -> rollback cycles more than 1 time within 24h (cooldown functioning)
- Safety: no correlated/mass rollback incidents (e.g., >5 tenants rolling back within 10 minutes) unless caused by confirmed shared infra incident; if detected, pause expansion + consider enabling global_disable
- Customer impact:
  - Reduction in MTTR vs manual intervention in at least 2 incidents or game day scenarios
- On-call readiness:
  - Runbook link included in incident-bot message
  - On-call acknowledges they can identify reason (latency vs error; baseline compare; min traffic guard) from console verdict page

Stop conditions (automatic or operator-driven)
- Immediate enable global kill switch (rc.auto_rollback.global_disable=true) if any of:
  - Monitor outage or staleness causes widespread UNKNOWN or missing data
  - Unexpected rollback rate spike (e.g., >10 rollbacks/hour globally)
  - Rollbacks occur for tenants/routes not in allowlist (bug)
  - Audit logging failures persist (cannot meet attribution/compliance requirements)

Observability requirements for rollout
Dashboards/alerts to validate during each cohort:
- rollout-controller:
  - monitor_client.request_rate / error_rate / cache_hit_ratio
  - slo_evaluator.verdict_counts{healthy,unhealthy,unknown}
  - slo_evaluator.lag_seconds (p50/p95/p99)
  - rollback_executor.actions_total (by reason: latency, error, baseline_worse)
  - rollback_executor.idempotency_conflicts_total
  - rollback_executor.throttled_total (per-tenant)
- Alerting guidance:
  - Page SRE only on: global kill switch engaged OR rollback spike OR monitor outage affecting verdict computation
  - Create ticket for: isolated tenant flapping or repeated UNKNOWN verdicts for a single route

Rollout operations checklist
Pre-rollout (C0/C1)
- [ ] Confirm monitor identity contract migration progress for cohort routes (ENG-2322)
- [ ] Validate integration tests passing in CI (ENG-2320)
- [ ] Confirm audit events emitted and visible in audit log explorer (ENG-2317)
- [ ] Confirm console verdict/rollback history page available behind console flag (ENG-2316)
- [ ] Run game day plan dry-run in staging (ENG-2323)

During rollout
- [ ] Enable verdicts_enabled for cohort
- [ ] Observe dashboards for 2–4 hours (then at 24h)
- [ ] Review a sample of decision traces for top routes (ensure min traffic + warm-up logic is behaving)
- [ ] Enable execution_enabled for cohort (only after Phase A criteria met)
- [ ] Enable notifications_enabled last (once paging noise risk is understood)

Post-rollout
- [ ] Document any false positives and adjust default policy recommendations (coord w/ SRE)
- [ ] Update runbook and on-call training notes

Rollback plan (for the feature)
If we need to roll back the auto-rollback feature (not the model rollout), we will:
1) Immediately set rc.auto_rollback.global_disable=true (kills execution).
2) Optionally keep rc.auto_rollback.verdicts_enabled=true for debugging; otherwise set false to reduce monitoring load.
3) Set rc.auto_rollback.notifications_enabled=false to stop paging.
4) Confirm no in-flight executor actions:
   - executor should be idempotent and respect kill switch at action time; verify by checking rollback_executor.actions_total stops increasing.
5) Comms:
   - Post in #eng-oncall and #eng-platform with reason + current state
   - If any customer-facing impact occurred, open incident/ticket and notify CS owner.
6) Code rollback (only if necessary): revert to prior stable rollout-controller build via standard deployment pipeline; keep config flags disabled to prevent re-trigger during rollback.

Open questions
- Do we want a tenant_blocklist for fast exclusion during broad rollout (vs reverting to allowlist)?
- Confirm exact cap for "mass rollback" detection: should it be N tenants/10m OR N rollbacks/10m, and should it be per-region?
- Default order for enabling notifications vs execution for C2 (SRE preference is notifications AFTER first execution cohort proves stable).

Latest updates
- 2025-02-18 (Connor O'Brien): Drafted initial flag set + cohort plan. Waiting on SRE sign-off on stop conditions (mass rollback threshold) and whether we allow fail_closed mode at all in v1.
- 2025-02-20 (Miles Thornton): Requested we keep notifications off until we have 48h of execution data; also asked for explicit "UNKNOWN" verdict handling requirements in plan (added above).
- 2025-02-21 (Rafael Mendes): On-call wants paging only on kill-switch activation and sustained rollback spikes; otherwise ticket. Need to confirm incident-bot templates include runbook + console links before C2.

Acceptance criteria
- Flags are documented with names, defaults, and precedence.
- Cohorts and enablement sequence are defined (Phase A + Phase B) with clear eligibility.
- Expand/stop criteria are explicit and measurable via dashboards/metrics.
- Rollback plan for the feature itself is documented and executable by on-call.
- Plan reviewed/approved by Release Eng (Connor), SRE (Rafael/Miles), and PM (Paula/Marissa) in comments.
